topic: Neutron stars: density, spin speed, tiny mountains, gold from collisions
hook: A teaspoon of neutron star weighs a billion tons

slides.title: A teaspoon of neutron star weighs a billion tons
slides.body: Neutron stars squeeze more than our Sun's mass into a ball only about 20 km wide.
slides.image_prompt: A tiny glowing silver teaspoon holding a blazing blue-white star fragment, floating in deep space above a small city skyline for scale
slides.credit: Credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/Southampton/W. Ho et al.; Illustration: NASA/CXC/M.Weiss (Public domain) via wikimedia

slides.title: They spin insanely fast
slides.body: The fastest one known turns 716 times every second, faster than a kitchen blender.
slides.image_prompt: A dense glowing sphere spinning rapidly in space, twin beams of light sweeping out from its poles like a cosmic lighthouse

slides.title: Mountains under 1 mm
slides.body: Their gravity is so extreme that the tallest bumps on the crust are likely less than a millimeter high.
slides.image_prompt: An extremely smooth, perfectly polished metallic sphere glowing faintly blue in black space, its surface almost flawless

slides.title: Crashes that forge gold
slides.body: In 2017, telescopes watched two neutron stars collide and create heavy elements like gold and platinum.
slides.image_prompt: Two bright stars spiraling into each other in space, exploding in a golden flash with glittering gold dust spraying outward

caption:
A single teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth. That is more than every car on the planet put together. These dead stars pack more than the Sun's mass into a city-sized ball.

Part 2 drops tomorrow: magnetars, the strongest magnets in the universe. Follow so the next weird fact finds you. Source: NASA.
